say: Four hikers are lost in a forest.
A predator is nearby. Each hiker has one camera.
At 10 metres, the detector finds the bear. In thick fog, it reports an elephant.
At 30 metres, it finds nothing.
Calibrated detection range: about 15 metres.
Does sharing what each hiker sees help them get out?
Each camera view feeds one shared, living map. Old sightings fade.
A teammate's report tells a hiker where to look closer, with a 3 times zoom.
Clear air: bear found at 20 metres. Light fog: missed.
Same forest, same predator, same random seed. Run twice.
Left: each hiker keeps a private map. Right: one shared map.
Sightings, exits and explored ground reach every hiker. Old evidence fades.
Only a separate evaluator holds ground truth. The hikers never see it.
Solo: 2 of 4 got out. Shared map: 4 of 4. A selected example, not the average.
Every pixel step runs on Open C V 5. YOLO X S runs on the new D N N engine.
Look closer defogs and zooms. Stereo S G B M computes depth from the stereo pair.
Dense odometry failed on foliage. O R B features and solve P n P RANSAC track each hiker.
Predictions were committed first. Then 159,800 calibrated episodes ran on A W S Graviton.
In clear air, sharing raised the escape rate from 27% to 42%.
Sharing beat solo in all 56 settings, at every fog level tested.
One prediction was partly wrong: shared sightings kept helping against a predator that senses the whole forest.
On uncertain sightings, an L L M agent calls Open C V tools.
It queries the map, checks for motion, and looks closer: bear 0.16 becomes bear 0.58.
It orders an escape. The evaluator confirms a real bear.
A human ranger approves every escape order. If the model fails, the rule decides.
The agent is not more accurate than the rule: fewer false alarms, more missed bears in thick fog.
A W S: Graviton for sweeps, an L 40 S G P U for the agent, Lambda for the viewer.
G P U spend is capped at $10; about 2 dollars 60 used. G P U instances stop themselves.
Solo: 27% got out. Shared map: 42%.
Lost Together. All simulated. Every prediction reported.
